translation:
Treats films.

Take an unlimited amount of light-bamboo shell, wipe off the fuzz with a cloth, burn it to ash while preserving its nature. For each qian of the medicine add three to five li of musk, grind together into fine powder, and apply it on the film; it is also excellent.

In treating all external-barrier eyes, one must never use knife, needle, hook, or cutting, for fear of injuring the blood of the eye, which would later become a chronic disease that cannot be treated. The Classic says, "The eye, obtaining blood, is able to see." Then how can the blood be damaged? Only use the Jinye, Yuhua, and similar formulas, and it will cure itself.

One: whenever a flying thread enters the eye, hold a grain of salt in the mouth and let it dissolve, and the thread will come out by itself. Or put one grain of fragrant-grass seed into the eye; the seed moves about within the eye, and wiping and drawing out the thread, it will cure itself.

One: whenever the mouth and eye are drawn askew, take several doses of wind-dispelling medicine; when the pulse is even, then take warming and tonifying medicine, and externally grind Baiji with eel blood and apply it to one side of the face, and one will immediately see the countenance become upright.
translator_notes: 淡竹殼 (light-bamboo shell) is the shell of the light bamboo, used here as a medicine.
存性 (cunxing) means preserving the nature of the medicine while burning it.
刀針鉤割 (knife, needle, hook, cutting) refers to surgical operations on the eye.
香草子 (fragrant-grass seed) cannot be identified with certainty.
